source.title: From Charts to Atlas: Merging Latent Spaces into One
source.authors: Donato Crisostomi; Irene Cannistraci; Luca Moschella; Pietro Barbiero; Marco Ciccone; Pietro Lió; E. Rodolà

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity with CKA after converting task-specific latent spaces to relative representations and aggregating them. It tests whether this produces spaces similar to an end-to-end model, and varies task overlap; it does not use a scale sweep or the original claim’s proposed cross-modal comparison.
record.gate_note: Rows record CKA comparisons of aggregated spaces with end-to-end spaces, including separately reported shared and non-shared subsets. Classification accuracy, separability, and the subclass experiment are not rows because they do not measure alignment between representations. The paper also describes PCA visualizations as similar, but does not report a separate numeric result for them.
record.test_reason: The study's CKA results compare relative-representation spaces of task-specific models, trained on overlapping or disjoint subsets of CIFAR100 and TinyImageNet, with an end-to-end model of the same architecture. These results bear on V4 (spaces become comparable via relative representations) and on how alignment varies with shared training data (V6, V7). The main aim is a merging method (RLSA), so this is a new-setting result rather than a replication. There is no scale, cross-modal or seed comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude relative representations enable merging latent spaces into a space similar to an end-to-end model's. Merging works best with a shared region but still gives good results for disjoint tasks. Against naive merging, the gains shrink in that case. The aggregated space's higher classification accuracy is attributed to task-specific footprints in the embeddings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses relative representations, cosine similarity to anchors, and averaging to aggregate task spaces; compares the resulting space with an end-to-end space using CKA. It does not reproduce the original sources’ methods or scale comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported CKA differs with task configuration and between shared and non-shared classes. The authors state that similarity decreases for class- and sample-disjoint tasks.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurReps; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 2023
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The experiments use CIFAR100 and TinyImageNet image-classification tasks; they do not test model scaling, cross-modal alignment, or alternative similarity metrics. The claimed influence of shared regions is shown across task configurations but is not isolated as a causal factor.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports other measures, including classification accuracy, class separability, and subclass-classification accuracy, but these do not measure representation alignment for the listed versions. Section 4.2 and 4.3 also report CKA values for disjoint-task settings, which are not included because the 60-row limit was reached by retaining every Table 1 CKA subset result.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability sweep. Every comparison is between models of the same architecture.
Models differ in training data subset, not only in seed. There is no same-data, different-seed comparison.

No cross-architecture mapping, stitching or unpaired mapping. CKA is computed for an aggregated relative space, not for a direct one-to-one map between two models. Mapping loss is not measured by transfer performance.
No feature, neuron or circuit analysis.
Only linear CKA is used; no alternative metrics or metric settings are compared. Input dependence is tested only as shared versus non-shared class subsets.
No plateau with scale. The shared-data effect is confounded with anchors being drawn from shared samples.

record.verdict_notes: Borderline between tests and T4: the CKA values are partly a performance score for the authors' merging method. They are kept as a test because they do measure agreement between independently trained models' relative spaces. Caveats: every comparison is within one architecture. Anchors in Exp. 1 come from shared samples, which confounds the V7 shared-data reading. Disjoint-task CKAs (Sec 4.2: 0.83–0.87 CIFAR100, 0.79–0.84 TinyImageNet; Sec 4.3: 0.81–0.83 CIFAR100, 0.72–0.81 TinyImageNet) are declared in rows_left_out. They show alignment persisting without shared data, which tempers the V7 reading and should ideally be added as rows. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no test of alignment increasing with scale or capability across independently trained models.
No vision-language comparison or paired image-caption representations.
Does not compare models trained from different initializations on the same task to test shared features or subspaces.

Tests relative-representation aggregation and CKA similarity to an end-to-end model, not whether a single simple map or stitched layers transfer representations with little loss, nor mapping without paired data.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, circuits, or SAE features.
Tests sensitivity to task/sample/class overlap using CKA. Does not compare similarity metrics or metric settings, and does not test out-of-distribution inputs as a convergence measure.
Tests how measured similarity varies with task overlap. Does not isolate shared training data or objectives as causal explanations, or test a scale-dependent plateau.

relationships.condition: Relative-representation aggregation, CIFAR100 (both models) and TinyImageNet VanillaCNN, with a sizeable shared class core
relationships.reason: CKA with the end-to-end space is 0.80–0.93 in most settings (e.g. r01–r03, r13–r15, r25–r27, r49–r51). Relative spaces of task models largely match the full model's.
relationships.display_finding: Aggregated task representations achieved CKA 0.80–0.93 with the end-to-end space in most tested settings.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Relative-representation aggregation, CIFAR100 (both models) and TinyImageNet VanillaCNN, with a sizeable shared class core
source_check.reason: Table 1 reports strong aggregated-to-global similarity in these settings; section 4.1 also reports preserved or improved downstream classification and separability.

relationships.condition: EfficientNet on TinyImageNet, and few shared classes (S=20) on CIFAR100
relationships.reason: CKA falls to 0.67–0.79: 0.67 and 0.72 for TinyImageNet non-shared classes (r58, r55), 0.74 for VanillaCNN S=20 non-shared (r10). Similarity after relative aggregation is far from lossless.
relationships.display_finding: CKA fell to 0.67–0.79, including 0.67 and 0.72 for non-shared TinyImageNet classes and 0.74 for non-shared CIFAR100 classes with 20 shared classes.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: EfficientNet on TinyImageNet, and few shared classes (S=20) on CIFAR100
source_check.reason: Similarity is reduced in these conditions: r55=0.72, r58=0.67 and r10=0.74. Aggregation remains useful, but representational equivalence is incomplete.

relationships.condition: Inputs restricted to shared versus task-specific (non-shared) classes
relationships.reason: Measured CKA is consistently lower on non-shared-class inputs than on shared ones (e.g. 0.74 vs 0.86 r10/r11; 0.67 vs 0.80 r58/r59). It weakens but does not vanish.

tranche.reason: Tests relative-representation aggregation in a new setting of partially overlapping and disjoint classification tasks, with CKA comparisons to a model trained on the whole dataset.

source_check.notes: CKA compares the aggregated relative space with the global model's space, rather than directly establishing pairwise model interchangeability. Section 4.1's assertion that all values exceed 0.7 conflicts with Table 1's 0.67; the recorded numeric value correctly follows the table.

statements.correction: Table 1: VanillaCNN, CIFAR100, S=20, N=10: non-shared CKA=0.74; shared CKA=0.86. EfficientNet, TinyImageNet, S=50, N=25: non-shared CKA=0.67; shared CKA=0.80. Input-dependent weakening supports V6.
statements.problem: The numbers and residual-alignment description are correct, but limits_scope misclassifies this study's evidence for V6. V6 explicitly permits weakening without disappearance.
